title: IMF says AI investment keeps global growth around 3%, with major Asia benefits
source_used: Reuters wire story, read in Yahoo Finance's copy (Reuters page itself returns HTTP 401)
key_facts: IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva said on Monday 12 Oct 2026, the first day of the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok, that strong AI infrastructure investment is keeping global growth at around 3%.

She said the AI investment boom is a "demand shock, an investment shock" that could add half to one full percentage point to growth in advanced Asian economies and 0.2 to 0.8 point in emerging Asian economies.
She said growth holds at around 3% despite being "dragged down by the energy supply shock".
The IMF forecast global growth at 3% for 2026 in July and will release an updated outlook on Tuesday.
She called AI a "slow-moving tsunami" for jobs, growth, education and taxation, and said the IMF estimates 40% of jobs could be augmented, downgraded or eliminated over time.
An initial study showed 10% of US jobs already require AI skills; low-paying jobs are growing in construction and data centres.
World Bank president Ajay Banga backed "small AI" for farmers, health and education; Singapore's president Tharman Shanmugaratnam warned that graduates face less demand for first jobs.
quote_evidence: The IMF in July forecast global growth at 3% in 2026.
The IMF estimates that AI could lead to 40% of jobs being augmented, downgraded or eliminated, over time, she said.

The US, China and India are the most important producers in the AI supply chain, but many of the firms building the needed infrastructure are in Asia, Georgieva said, referencing Thailand, host of this year's annual meetings.
why_it_matters_hint: The head of the IMF says AI spending is what keeps world growth near 3%, while warning of large effects on jobs and tax revenue.
notes: Reuters page blocked (401); the same Reuters text was read in the Yahoo Finance copy. Also carried by Business Standard, The Economic Times and others. The growth effects are her estimates.
